newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Bank of Israel cancels monetary tenders.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Israel cancels monetary tenders.

text.p: The Bank of Israel said it had cancelled its Monday monetary tender to commercial banks and would not hold another tender until further notice because of too much liquidity in the system.
The tender is for daily loans to commercial banks.
Last month the central bank cancelled seven such tenders because of surplus liquidity and in July the central bank's weekly tenders to commercial banks were cancelled.
In a statement the central bank said it would issue a notice when the daily tenders are resumed.
The excess liquidity is a result of high government expenditure, the statement said.

On Sunday the Treasury said the government's deficit in August had soared to 2.089 billion shekels against a deficit of 879 million in July. In the first eight months of the year the Treasury reported a government deficit of 8.6 billion shekels, already above the deficit target of 7.6 billion shekels for the entire year.
